claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can form a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy-alloy solid solution.
The initial alloy can be annealed into a random solid solution without long-range order or incipient SRO.
Controlled annealing or MD quenching can tune SRO from a random distribution through isolated clusters to a continuous percolating network while preserving a single BCC phase.
BCC refractory HEAs can possess a significant energetic driving force for chemical SRO.
At 0.5 Tm to 0.8 Tm, anharmonicity is significant.
The alloy remains thermodynamically stable as a single-phase BCC solid solution without secondary phases throughout the stated high-temperature regime.
Composition and annealing temperature can cause HEAs to decompose into multiple phases.
SRO produces Nb-Ta-rich or Hf-Zr-rich clusters in HfNbTaTiZr.
At sufficient SRO, chemically ordered clusters form a continuous percolating network.
At low SRO, mass variance and local strain fields increase phonon scattering and reduce thermal conductivity.
Percolation of SRO clusters creates a connected sub-lattice with reduced local potential-energy fluctuations.
The connected ordered sub-lattice provides a coherent, low-scattering propagation pathway for high-frequency phonons.
Reduced high-frequency phonon scattering after percolation causes a sharp increase in thermal conductivity.
Thermal conductivity has a non-monotonic dependence on SRO, initially decreasing and then rising sharply at percolation.
At the percolative upturn, thermal conductivity exceeds that of the random solid solution at the same temperature.
Standard Debye-Callaway or Allen-Feldman treatments with independent point-defect scattering predict a monotonic conductivity decrease as SRO increases.
The proposed conductivity upturn violates standard Matthiessen's-rule predictions.
The magnitude and threshold of the proposed upturn depend strongly on whether the interatomic potential accurately represents the energetic driving force and evolution of SRO.
Current interatomic potentials may not accurately predict SRO evolution in HfNbTaTiZr.

A DFT-trained, system-specific machine-learned potential, Green-Kubo conductivity calculations, SRO measurements, and cluster-connectivity analysis can test whether the conductivity change coincides with percolation rather than isolated-cluster scattering.
